title_en: ICI’s Antoniewicz on Active’s Changing Landscape
title_zh: ICI 首席经济学家 Antoniewicz：主动管理正在改变的格局
subtitle_zh: 美国投资公司协会（ICI）首席经济学家 Shelly Antoniewicz 做客彭博行业研究 David Cohne 的 Inside Active，谈主动管理为何“改变形态”而非消亡：主动型 ETF 与主动债基的净流入、资金流数据的局限、共同基金在 401(k) 中的韧性与 CIT 的崛起、份额类别与《GROWTH 法案》的影响，以及费率长期下行的驱动力。
summary_zh: 本期 Inside Active 由 Bloomberg Intelligence 的 David Cohne 主持，对话美国投资公司协会（Investment Company Institute，ICI）首席经济学家 Shelly Antoniewicz，宏观审视主动管理改变形态而非消亡的格局。Antoniewicz 用数据反驳主动已死：截至 7 月底，主动型共同基金与 ETF 合计管理资产超 18 万亿美元，较十年前的 11 万亿增长近 70%；过去两年半主动型 ETF 净流入 1.2 万亿美元、主动型债券共同基金另有 3,000 亿美元净流入。她强调主动与指数并非零和而是互补——投资者可用指数股基作核心、以主动债基灵活调整久期，收费型顾问（fee-based advisors）更以指数基金为模块构建高度主动的模型组合。她提醒资金流是总量指标，会掩盖底层活动（一买一卖净额为零却交易活跃），也受奖金、报税、资本利得分配等季节性因素影响，不宜过度解读短期轮动。节目还谈到共同基金向 ETF 迁移、401(k) 中因券商窗口稀缺而 ETF 受限、集合投资信托（CIT）在大型计划中的崛起、ETF 份额类别与《GROWTH 法案》（GROWTH Act）的潜在影响、费率长期下行的三大驱动力（规模、成本敏感度、竞争）及其趋缓而非触底，以及代币化（tokenization）与 AI 可能重塑未来的交付方式。
description: ICI’s Antoniewicz on Active’s Changing Landscape

turns.en: Welcome to Inside Active, a podcast about active managers that goes beyond soundbites and headlines and looks deeper into their processes, challenges, and philosophies in security selection. I'm David Cohn. I lead mutual fund and active research at Bloomberg Intelligence. Active management has undergone a significant transformation over the past decade. Investors have continued to move money away from actively managed mutual funds, while active ETFs have grown rapidly and fund expenses have continued to decline. At the same time, changes in financial advice, distribution, and investor preferences are reshaping how active management is packaged and delivered. That means the traditional active versus passive debate may not tell the whole story. Understanding where active management is headed also requires looking at the vehicles investors are choosing, what they're willing to pay, and how those choices differ across investors and distribution channels. Today, I wanted to take a broader look at those trends. What's driving the shift between mutual funds and ETFs? What fund flows can and can't tell us about investor behavior? How the economics of active management are changing? And what all of this could mean for the future of the industry? Joining me to discuss that is Shelley Antonavich, Chief Economist at the Investment Company Institute. Shelley, thanks for joining me.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 Inside Active，这是一档关于主动管理型投资人的播客，我们不满足于金句和标题，而是更深入地探究他们在证券选择上的流程、挑战与投资理念。我是 David Cohne，负责彭博行业研究（Bloomberg Intelligence）的共同基金与主动管理研究。过去十年，主动管理经历了重大转变。投资者持续把资金从主动管理型共同基金中撤出，而主动型 ETF 迅速增长，基金费用则不断下降。与此同时，财务顾问服务、分销渠道和投资者偏好的变化，正在重塑主动管理的包装方式与交付方式。这意味着，传统的“主动对被动”之争可能并未讲出全部真相。要理解主动管理将走向何方，还需要观察投资者正在选择什么样的产品载体、他们愿意为此支付多少费用，以及这些选择在不同投资者和不同分销渠道之间存在怎样的差异。今天，我想更宏观地审视这些趋势：是什么在驱动资金从共同基金转向 ETF？基金资金流能告诉我们、又不能告诉我们哪些关于投资者行为的信息？主动管理的经济学正在如何改变？以及这一切对行业的未来可能意味着什么？今天与我一起讨论这些话题的，是美国投资公司协会（Investment Company Institute，ICI）首席经济学家 Shelly Antoniewicz。Shelly，感谢你的到来。

turns.en: Hi, thanks so much for having me. I'm really thrilled to be here today.
turns.zh: 你好，非常感谢邀请我。今天能来到这里，我真的很高兴。

turns.en: So, you know, when you look across ICI's data, how would you characterize the state of active management today? What, you know, what stands out most about how active management is evolving?
turns.zh: 那么，纵观 ICI 的数据，你会如何描述当前主动管理的状态？在主动管理的演变过程中，最突出的是什么？

turns.en: Well, I think you hit the nail on the head. You know, I agree with you. I would characterize active management today as being in this period of transformation. You know, I know there's narratives out there that say active management is quote unquote dead. You know, I completely disagree with those. First, you know, there's the sheer size. Actively managed mutual funds and ETFs collectively had over $ 18 trillion in assets under management at the end of July. That's up almost 70% from $ 11 trillion a decade ago. So definitely not shrinking. Second, active ETFs and active bond mutual funds are thriving. In just the last two and a half years alone, actively managed ETFs have seen $ 1. 2 trillion and active bond mutual funds another $ 300 billion in net new money come into their funds. Third, I think more indexing absolutely does not mean less active management. You know, if you think about fee-based advisors, that's one example. Fee-based advisors have taken a more active role in managing their clients' assets through the use of allocation models or model portfolios, and they're implementing these active strategies using index funds. So while an advisor may select an index fund, their client's overall portfolio construction tactical allocations, tax management, and rebalancing are often highly active. So in sum, for me, the industry's evolution is not about investors abandoning active management. It's about active management changing form.
turns.zh: 嗯，我觉得你说到点子上了，我同意你的看法。我会把今天的主动管理描述为正处于一个转型期。我知道外界有一种说法，称主动管理已经“死了”。我完全不认同。首先是规模：截至 7 月底，主动管理型共同基金和 ETF 合计管理资产超过 18 万亿美元，比十年前的 11 万亿美元增长了近 70%。所以绝对没有在萎缩。其次，主动型 ETF 和主动型债券共同基金正蓬勃发展。仅在过去两年半时间里，主动管理型 ETF 就有 1.2 万亿美元的净新增资金流入，主动型债券共同基金另有 3000 亿美元净流入。第三，我认为指数化程度的提高绝不意味着主动管理的减少。以收费型投资顾问（fee-based advisors）为例：他们通过资产配置模型或模型组合，在管理客户资产时扮演了更加主动的角色，而他们在实施这些主动策略时使用的是指数基金。所以，虽然顾问可能选择了一只指数基金，但其客户整体组合的构建、战术配置、税务管理和再平衡往往高度主动。总之，在我看来，这个行业的演进并不是投资者在抛弃主动管理，而是主动管理在改变形态。

turns.en: Now you make a good point. And I kind of want to go back to the end there when you talk about index investing, because I think when a lot of people talk about the growth of passive investing, you know, what was happening kind of before the whole recent surge in active, you know, we often treat active and passive as competing for the same dollar. But, you know, from ICI's research, it sounds like the investor or advisor behavior isn't that straightforward.
turns.zh: 你说得有道理。我想回到你结尾谈到指数投资的部分，因为我觉得当很多人谈到被动投资的增长——也就是在近期这波主动管理热潮兴起之前发生的情况时，我们常常把主动和被动当作在争夺同一笔资金。但从 ICI 的研究来看，投资者或顾问的行为似乎并没有这么简单。

turns.en: No, from my perspective, I don't believe the industry is a zero-sum competition between active and index. Active and index are complements and definitely can work together within an investor's portfolio. So for You know, these are just examples I'm going to use. An investor may have index equity funds as their core holdings, but for their fixed income exposure, they select an active bond fund. Why would they want to do this? Active bond funds have more flexibility to set and adjust their duration, and that is particularly useful if interest rates are on the rise because that can help mitigate losses by reducing their duration. Or think about an investor who wants exposure to alternatives like private assets. Retail alternatives are generally still an active management business with strategies requiring specialized research or active risk management.
turns.zh: 不，在我看来，我不认为这个行业是主动与指数之间的零和竞争。主动和指数是互补的，完全可以在一位投资者的组合中协同发挥作用。下面这些只是我要举的例子：一位投资者可能把指数型股票基金作为核心持仓，但在固定收益敞口上选择一只主动型债券基金。为什么要这么做？主动型债券基金在设定和调整久期方面有更大的灵活性，这在利率上行时尤其有用，因为可以通过缩短久期来帮助减轻损失。或者，想想一位希望获得另类资产（比如私募资产）敞口的投资者。面向零售投资者的另类资产基本上仍是一门主动管理的生意，其策略需要专门的研究或主动的风险管理。

turns.en: Now, you make a good point there. You know, I'm still waiting for the day when privates do become passive. And I think they'll be kind of interesting and complicated, but be fun to watch. Yeah. Another thing I wanted to ask, you know, we often use fund flows as a measure of investor preferences. How much do you think we can actually infer about investor behavior from flows? And you think those numbers, we can kind of miss something from those numbers?
turns.zh: 你这一点说得很好。我还在等着私募资产变得被动化的那一天，我想那会既有趣又复杂，但值得一看。是的。我还想问一个问题：我们常常用基金资金流来衡量投资者偏好。你认为我们究竟能从资金流中推断出多少投资者行为的信息？你觉得我们是否会从这些数字里漏掉一些东西？

turns.en: Flows can tell us a lot about changes in investor preferences or their risk appetites, but we have to be really careful not to over-interpret them. So, you know, some flow patterns are definitely reflect short-term influences, such as like bonus payments or capital gains distributions or tax deadlines. And these induce seasonality in the flows. You know, one example is funds tend to have above average inflows in the first few months of the year as people invest their annual bonuses or make contributions to their IRS. I'll often, I do a lot of press interviews and I'll have reporters sort of want to talk to me after they see one week of, you know, inflows into equity funds and outflows from bond funds. And they'll say, oh, is this the start of the rotation? And I want to say to them, come back to me in about six months. And if we've seen this pattern over six months, then we can talk about that. You know, other flow trends reflect longer term forces, such as demographics, retirement savings patterns or even changes in product preferences. We've seen that. The aging of the baby boom generation is often cited as contributing to the strong demand for bond funds that we've seen over the past 15 years. I think just as important to looking at short-term fluctuations, long-term influences, I think what's just as important to keep in mind is that the flow data, Particularly the data ICI publishes are an aggregate measure. And they can mask a great deal of underlying activity. So let me just give you a really simple example. You can have one investor sell $ 1, 000 of a fund while another investor buys $ 1, 000 of the same fund, say. Well, you know, the net flow here is zero, which... you'd say, okay, nothing happened. But in reality, there was significant trading if those were the only two trades the fund had. There was significant trading and potentially very different investor motivations and viewpoints. That's why I think VLOs are sort of best used as a useful signal rather than a complete picture of investor behavior.
turns.zh: 资金流能告诉我们很多关于投资者偏好或风险偏好变化的信息，但我们必须非常谨慎，不要过度解读。有些资金流模式确实反映的是短期因素，比如奖金发放、资本利得分配或报税截止日，这些因素会给资金流带来季节性。举个例子，年初的头几个月基金往往会出现高于平均水平的资金流入，因为人们会把年度奖金投入市场，或者向自己的 IRA 账户供款。我经常接受媒体采访，记者们看到某一周股票基金出现资金流入、债券基金出现资金流出之后就想来找我聊，他们会问：“哦，这是轮动的开始吗？”我想对他们说，六个月后再来找我。如果我们在六个月里都看到了这种模式，那时我们再来讨论。另一些资金流趋势反映的是更长期的力量，比如人口结构、退休储蓄模式，甚至是产品偏好的变化。我们已经看到，婴儿潮一代的老龄化常被认为是过去 15 年债券基金需求强劲的原因之一。我认为，与关注短期波动和长期影响同样重要的一点是：资金流数据——尤其是 ICI 发布的数据——是一个总量指标，它可能掩盖大量的底层活动。我举一个非常简单的例子：一位投资者卖出某只基金 1,000 美元，同时另一位投资者买入同一只基金 1,000 美元，那么这里的净流量为零，你会说“好吧，什么都没发生”。但实际上，如果这只基金只有这两笔交易，那么交易是相当活跃的，而且两位投资者的动机和观点可能截然不同。这就是为什么我认为资金流最好被当作一个有用的信号，而不是投资者行为的完整图景。

turns.en: No, it makes a lot of sense. You know, I do want to, you know, I know everyone talks about mutual funds versus ETFs. And, you know, the industry is kind of increasingly choosing ETFs over mutual funds in a lot of places. And, you know, I'm just curious how much we can attribute that to cost, taxes, and trading flexibility, which, you know, we've already heard is like the benefits of ETFs versus actually, you know, how financial advice is being delivered today.
turns.zh: 不，这很有道理。我确实想谈一谈——我知道所有人都在讨论共同基金与 ETF 之争，而且行业在很多领域正越来越多地选择 ETF 而非共同基金。我很好奇，这在多大程度上可以归因于成本、税务和交易灵活性（我们已经听过这些是 ETF 的优势），又在多大程度上其实是因为如今财务顾问服务的交付方式发生了变化？

turns.en: So you're right. ETFs are increasingly popular with retail investors. We've done surveys for many, many years looking at, you know, ownership of mutual funds, ownership of ETFs. And in 2015, our survey showed that just 5% of U.S. households owned ETFs. As of 2025, we estimate that 15% or 20 million U.S. households owned ETFs. And I expect when we publish our 2026 figure next month, that's going to be even higher. You know, as for the factors influencing or driving the demand for ETFs, it's really hard to rank them by their sort of relative importance. In our surveys, you know, around 95% of ETF owners cite cost-effectiveness and diversification as the top reasons for why they invest in ETFs. And about... 90% said they appreciated the tax efficiency and the ability to trade during the day. You know, we do know that more brokers and financial advisors are using ETFs in their clients' portfolios. If you look at, data from 2014, fee-based advisors had 17% of their clients' household assets invested in ETFs. Roll forward 10 years to 2024, that ETF share is up to 49%. And I'm likely is still rising. We'll get a read on the 2025 data this fall. So we'll be able to update that stat. But what I think is this shift reflects something I mentioned earlier, that fee-based advisors are increasingly using model portfolios that have index funds, and it's predominantly index ETFs as their building blocks.
turns.zh: 你说得对，ETF 在零售投资者中越来越受欢迎。我们做关于共同基金持有情况、ETF 持有情况的调查已经很多很多年了。2015 年，我们的调查显示只有 5% 的美国家庭持有 ETF；到 2025 年，我们估计这一比例为 15%，也就是 2,000 万个美国家庭持有 ETF。我预计下个月我们发布 2026 年数据时，这个数字还会更高。至于影响或驱动 ETF 需求的因素，很难按相对重要性给它们排序。在我们的调查中，大约 95% 的 ETF 持有者把成本效益和分散化列为他们投资 ETF 的首要原因，约 90% 表示他们看重税收效率以及盘中交易的能力。我们确实知道，越来越多的券商和财务顾问在客户组合中使用 ETF。看 2014 年的数据，收费型顾问的客户家庭资产中有 17% 投资于 ETF；往后十年到 2024 年，这一 ETF 占比上升到 49%，而且很可能仍在上升。今年秋天我们会拿到 2025 年的数据读数，届时就能更新这一统计。但我认为，这种转变反映了我前面提到的一点：收费型顾问越来越多地使用模型组合，而这些模型组合的构建模块是指数基金，并且以指数型 ETF 为主。

turns.en: That's interesting. We talk a lot about the whole mutual fund ETF shift as if every investor and every distribution channel is just moving in the same direction. Where do you think mutual funds remain particularly durable and what would explain that resilience?
turns.zh: 这很有意思。我们大量讨论共同基金向 ETF 的转移，仿佛每一位投资者、每一条分销渠道都在朝同一个方向移动。你认为共同基金在哪些领域仍然特别稳固？是什么解释了这种韧性？

turns.en: So one area where mutual funds remain especially durable is the defined contribution market. In a 401k plan, participants are typically making regular contributions every pay period. you know, often it's every two weeks. And they're, you know, relatively small amounts when you consider what sort of investments, you know, when you're making your investments. And mutual funds are particularly well suited to that environment because they can easily accommodate fractional share investing and they have seamless record keeping. Some features of the ETF that make ETFs attractive in taxable brokerage accounts are also less relevant in retirement plans. Intraday trading, for example, provides limited value to a long-term retirement saver making periodic contributions. Similarly, the tax efficiency often associated with ETFs are largely moot inside a tax-deferred retirement account.
turns.zh: 共同基金依然特别稳固的一个领域是固定缴存（defined contribution）计划市场。在 401(k) 计划中，参与者通常每个发薪期都会定期供款，往往是每两周一次，而且就你所做的投资而言，金额相对较小。共同基金特别适合这种环境，因为它们可以轻松支持碎股投资，而且记账无缝衔接。ETF 的一些让它在应税经纪账户中具有吸引力的特性，在退休计划中就不那么重要了。例如，盘中交易对于一位定期供款的长期退休储蓄者来说价值有限。同样，常与 ETF 联系在一起的税收效率，在税收递延的退休账户内部也基本失去意义。

turns.en: You know, one of the things, the big stories over the last year or so has been the share class. And I think a lot of folks were focusing on the ETF share class of the mutual fund, but also the mutual fund share class of the ETF is something. And so, you know, do you expect ETFs to eventually make greater inroads, whether that is with, you know, the mutual fund share class of an ETF? Or do you think there'll be more of CIT's domains?
turns.zh: 你知道，过去一年左右的大新闻之一就是份额类别（share class）。我认为很多人关注的是共同基金的 ETF 份额类别，但 ETF 的共同基金份额类别同样值得关注。那么，你是否预计 ETF 最终会取得更大的突破——无论是通过 ETF 的共同基金份额类别？还是你认为更多的会是集合投资信托（CIT）的地盘？

turns.en: Well, I think one challenge to widespread adoption of ETFs in 401ks is the need for a brokerage window. So even if you have an, you know, ETF share class of a mutual fund, you still have to have a brokerage window to get to that ETF because that ETF is trading on a secondary market. And so plan participants in order, you know, a defined contribution or 401k plan participants in order to get access to ETFs, they need that brokerage window. And because of cost consideration and operational hurdles, relatively few 401k plans have a brokerage window. I think you also asked about CITs.
turns.zh: 嗯，我认为 ETF 在 401(k) 中被广泛采用的一个挑战，是必须要有券商窗口（brokerage window）。所以，即使你有了共同基金的 ETF 份额类别，你仍然必须有一个券商窗口才能买到那只 ETF，因为那只 ETF 是在二级市场上交易的。因此，固定缴存计划或 401(k) 计划的参与者要想获得 ETF，就需要这个券商窗口。而由于成本考量和操作上的障碍，只有相对较少的 401(k) 计划设有券商窗口。我想你还问到了 CIT。

turns.en: Yes, yes.
turns.zh: 是的，是的。

turns.en: Yeah. So CITs have definitely, though, been gaining market share in large 401k plans. In 2024, which is the latest data we have available, 37% of large 401k plan assets were in CITs. And that's up from 12% in 2010. And, you know, while CITs and mutual funds operate similarly in many of our members, at ICI offer both products to 401k plan sponsors, CITs have a less burdensome regulatory structure. For example, they don't have as many disclosure documents to prepare and file, and they're often not subject to some of the same rules that mutual funds are. This translates into lower compliance costs for CITs, which they can use to competitively price their products.
turns.zh: 是的。不过 CIT 在大型 401(k) 计划中确实一直在抢占市场份额。在我们目前能获得的最新数据——2024 年中，大型 401(k) 计划资产的 37% 配置在 CIT 中，而 2010 年这一比例为 12%。虽然 CIT 和共同基金在很多方面运作方式相似——我们 ICI 的许多会员同时向 401(k) 计划发起人提供这两类产品——但 CIT 的监管结构负担更轻。例如，它们需要准备和提交的信息披露文件没有那么多，而且往往不受一些约束共同基金的同样规则的管辖。这就转化为 CIT 更低的合规成本，它们可以利用这一点为产品定出更有竞争力的价格。

turns.en: That makes sense. As ETFs do account for this growing share of the fund business, has that changed the competitive dynamics of the asset management industry itself? You know, who can compete, how firms distribute products, or even the scale needed to succeed?
turns.zh: 这说得通。随着 ETF 在基金业务中占据越来越大的份额，这是否改变了资产管理行业本身的竞争格局？比如谁能参与竞争、公司如何分销产品，甚至成功所需的规模？

turns.en: I think the first thing we need to remember is that the asset management industry has always been highly competitive. Firms have continually adapted to changes in investor preferences, distribution channels, technology, and product innovation. What's interesting is that competition is becoming less about the wrapper and more about delivering value to investors. So investors are looking for outcomes, exposures, advice, and efficient implementations. And whether those are delivered through a mutual fund, an ETF, a CIT, or some other structure, you know, they're really, you know, that isn't as critical to them. That said, one development that could prove, you know, especially significant is what you mentioned before, the ETF share class of a mutual fund. If ETF share classes become widely available, this could reduce some of the distinction between mutual funds and ETFs by allowing firms to offer both structures within the same fund. This would give investors more choice and potentially lower operational barriers for fund sponsors. You know, on the other hand, if the Growth Act, which levels the tax treatment of mutual funds and ETFs is approved by Congress, there could be more limited use of the ETF share class. It's interesting.
turns.zh: 我认为首先要记住的是，资产管理行业一直以来都是高度竞争的。各家机构不断适应投资者偏好、分销渠道、技术和产品创新的变化。有意思的是，竞争正变得不再那么关乎“外壳”（wrapper），而更多关乎为投资者创造价值。投资者追求的是投资结果、敞口、建议以及高效的实施；至于这些是通过共同基金、ETF、CIT 还是其他结构来交付，对他们来说其实并不那么关键。话虽如此，有一项发展可能格外重要，就是你之前提到的——共同基金的 ETF 份额类别。如果 ETF 份额类别被广泛提供，这可能会减少共同基金与 ETF 之间的部分差异，因为公司可以在同一只基金内提供两种结构。这将给投资者更多选择，并可能降低基金发起人的运营门槛。另一方面，如果《GROWTH 法案》（GROWTH Act，该法案将使共同基金与 ETF 的税收待遇趋于一致）获得国会通过，ETF 份额类别的使用可能会更为有限。这很有意思。

turns.en: I haven't thought about that. You know, if we kind of just stay on the topic of ETFs in general, do you see active ETFs primarily taking assets from active mutual funds or Are they expanding the addressable market for active management and potentially competing for assets that otherwise would have gone to index products?
turns.zh: 我还没想到这一点。那么，如果我们继续谈论 ETF 这个大话题：你认为主动型 ETF 主要是从主动型共同基金手中夺取资产，还是它们在扩大主动管理的可服务市场，并可能去争夺那些原本会流向指数产品的资产？

turns.en: I think it's probably a bit of both. Some of the growth in active ETFs is clearly coming from investors and asset managers migrating existing active strategies out of mutual funds and into an ETF wrapper. In those cases, the underlying investment philosophy hasn't changed. But investors may prefer the ETF's distribution, trading, or tax efficiency. But I also think active ETFs are expanding the addressable market for active management. Historically, investors who maybe preferred the ETF wrapper had more limited access to active strategies in that format. And as more active ETFs have come to market, investors who might have otherwise preferred chosen, say, an index ETF can now access active management in a vehicle that fits how they want to build their portfolio. This, I think, suggests that competition in the industry is not simply active ETF versus active mutual fund. I think increasingly active ETFs are competing across a broader landscape that includes index ETFs. And more broadly, this may be another example of why sort of the simple active versus passive narrative can be misleading. Investors often make decisions about vehicle structure, distribution channel, tax efficiency, or portfolio implementation first. Then they choose between an active and index exposure within sort of what they consider is their preferred structure. Okay.
turns.zh: 我认为两者可能都有一点。主动型 ETF 的部分增长显然来自投资者和资产管理人把现有的主动策略从共同基金迁移到 ETF 外壳中。在这些情况下，底层投资理念并没有改变，但投资者可能更偏好 ETF 的分销、交易或税收效率。但我也认为，主动型 ETF 正在扩大主动管理的可服务市场。过去，那些偏好 ETF 外壳的投资者能够以这种形式获得的主动策略较为有限。而随着更多主动型 ETF 上市，那些原本可能会选择指数型 ETF 的投资者，现在可以通过一种契合其组合构建方式的载体获得主动管理。我认为这表明，行业内的竞争并不简单地是主动型 ETF 与主动型共同基金之争；主动型 ETF 越来越多地在一个更广阔的战场上竞争，其中也包括指数型 ETF。更广泛地说，这可能是又一个例子，说明为什么简单的“主动对被动”叙事会产生误导。投资者往往先就产品载体结构、分销渠道、税收效率或组合实施做出决定，然后才在他们认为自己偏好的结构内部，在主动与指数敞口之间做出选择。好的。

turns.en: And I did want to, because I think ICI is particularly great with these type of things, is just your view on generational changes in fund ownerships. Obviously, it's been changing. Do you think that fund ownership could eventually change the types of products that dominate the industry if we go from generation to generation? Yeah.
turns.zh: 我还想问一个问题，因为我认为 ICI 在这类事情上特别擅长：你对基金持有结构的代际变化有什么看法？显然这一直在变化。你认为如果一代一代地看下去，基金持有结构最终会改变行业中占主导地位的产品类型吗？是的。

turns.en: So there are clear generational forces that continue to shape the industry over the long run. Some of the data that we have you know, shows that about one third of ETF owning households are millennials, and they're more likely to encounter ETFs through digital platforms and fee-based advisory relationships. And I think part of that is we got to remember these younger households are entering the financial markets through a very different ecosystem than previous generations. And these younger generations are tending to favor the ETF wrapper in their taxable accounts. That said, I'd be cautious about drawing a straight line from demographics to the future dominance of any single product. Different products tend to serve different investor needs and distribution channels. So, you know, we were just talking about the retirement space. You know, mutual funds and ETFs remain deeply embedded in retirement plans. While ETFs have become increasingly important in brokerage and advisory accounts. And so, you know, as younger cohorts accumulate wealth, we may continue to see strong demand for ETF-based solutions in their tech. accounts. But the larger trend is likely to be continued innovation across all the product structures.
turns.zh: 确实存在一些明显的代际力量，在长期内持续塑造这个行业。我们掌握的一些数据显示，持有 ETF 的家庭中约三分之一是千禧一代，他们更有可能通过数字平台和收费型顾问关系接触到 ETF。我认为其中一部分原因在于——我们要记住，这些较年轻的家庭进入金融市场的生态系统与前几代人非常不同，而这些年轻一代在其应税账户中往往更偏好 ETF 外壳。话虽如此，对于从人口结构直接推断出任何单一产品未来将占主导地位，我会持谨慎态度。不同产品往往服务于不同的投资者需求和分销渠道。比如我们刚才谈到的退休领域：共同基金和 ETF 在退休计划中仍然根深蒂固，而 ETF 在经纪账户和顾问账户中的重要性日益提升。因此，随着年轻群体积累财富，我们可能会继续看到他们的应税账户对基于 ETF 的解决方案有强劲需求。但更大的趋势可能是所有产品结构都将持续创新。

turns.en: It'll definitely be something to watch. And, you know, something else that we've been watching is fund expenses. And, you know, I think it's one of the The most striking long-term trend from ICI's research is this decline in fund expenses. What do you think has been the biggest force driving fees lower, particularly for actively managed funds?
turns.zh: 这绝对值得关注。我们一直在观察的另一件事是基金费用。我认为，ICI 研究中最引人注目的长期趋势之一就是基金费用的下降。你认为推动费率下行的最大力量是什么，尤其是对于主动管理型基金？

turns.en: Yeah, we publish an annual report on fund fees every year. And we look at index mutual funds, active mutual funds, index ETFs, active ETFs. It's a very detailed report. It comes out March, towards the end of March every year. And our report from this year showed that if you look at actively managed mutual funds, the average expense ratio for an equity active mutual fund has fallen 41% over the past 29 years. So that's quite a big decline. I mean, and that certainly benefits to investors in these funds. What are the factors that contribute to this decline? First, scale. Scale matters a lot because as funds grow and fixed costs are spread across a larger asset base, this reduces the cost of managing those assets and those savings are just passed on to investors through lower expense ratios. Second, investor sensitivity to cost has increased substantially. Investors, advisors, retirement plans, institutional clients are paying very close attention to fees. and they're creating strong incentives for active fund sponsors to keep costs competitive. Third, it's your classic competitive pressure. The rise of index mutual funds and index ETFs has intensified competition across the entire asset management industry. Even though actively managed funds and index funds can serve the same investors the same investor's needs, the availability of lower cost investment auctions has certainly pushed active managers to reduce expenses where possible. And then finally, even within the active fund universe, we see that money has increasingly flowed toward lower cost funds within the active managed space. So You know, investors aren't just simply choosing between active and index. They're often choosing among active funds with different cost structures.
turns.zh: 是的，我们每年都发布一份关于基金费率的年度报告，我们会考察指数型共同基金、主动型共同基金、指数型 ETF、主动型 ETF。这是一份非常详尽的报告，每年在 3 月底左右发布。我们今年的报告显示，就主动管理型共同基金而言，主动型股票共同基金的平均费用率在过去 29 年里下降了 41%。这是相当大的降幅，这些基金的投资者当然从中受益。促成这一下降的因素有哪些？第一，规模。规模非常重要，因为随着基金规模增长，固定成本被摊薄到更大的资产基数上，这就降低了管理这些资产的成本，而这些节省会通过更低的费用率传递给投资者。第二，投资者对成本的敏感度大幅提高。投资者、顾问、退休计划、机构客户都在非常密切地关注费率，这就给主动型基金发起人保持有竞争力的成本带来了强烈激励。第三，就是经典的竞争压力。指数型共同基金和指数型 ETF 的兴起加剧了整个资产管理行业的竞争。尽管主动管理型基金和指数基金可以满足同一位投资者的需求，但低成本投资选项的可得性确实促使主动管理人在可能的情况下降低费用。最后，即便在主动型基金内部，我们也看到资金越来越多地流向主动管理领域中成本更低的基金。所以投资者并不只是在主动与指数之间做选择，他们常常是在成本结构不同的主动型基金之间做选择。

turns.en: So do you think that the falling fees have narrowed, you know, I guess what we would consider a disadvantage for active managers? They have to not only beat their benchmark, but they also have to overcome a high fee. Do you think that's narrowed that or is it kind of, do you think the competition's really just reset what investors consider acceptable fees for active management?
turns.zh: 那么你认为，费率下降是否缩小了——我想我们可以称之为主动管理人的一项劣势：他们不仅要跑赢基准，还要克服高昂的费用。你认为这一点缩小了吗？还是说，竞争其实只是重置了投资者认为主动管理可以接受的费用水平？

turns.en: Well, you know, fees are just one component of an investor's decision. And I think we're going to talk a little bit later about besides cost, what else do investors value when they're looking to buy a fund? But all else equal, you're right. Lower fees make an actively managed fund more attractive because they reduce that performance hurdle that the manager needs to overcome. You know, At the same time, investors ultimately care about outcomes, and lower fees can help get an active strategy onto an investor shortlist. That said, active managers still need to deliver a compelling investment experience by demonstrating performance, risk management, or other forms of value.
turns.zh: 嗯，费用只是投资者决策的一个组成部分。我想我们稍后会谈到，除了成本之外，投资者在考虑购买基金时还看重什么。但在其他条件相同的情况下，你说得对：更低的费用会让一只主动管理型基金更具吸引力，因为它们降低了管理人需要跨越的业绩门槛。与此同时，投资者最终关心的是结果，而较低的费用可以帮助一项主动策略进入投资者的候选名单。话虽如此，主动管理人仍然需要通过展示业绩、风险管理或其他形式的价值，来提供有说服力的投资体验。

turns.en: To the investor. With fees, though, with an index fund, there's not a whole lot of money that a company... I mean, obviously, there is money to manage a fund in general. But with active, with fees, they help pay for research, portfolio management, distribution, and just all the rest of the business. So do you see signs that fee compression is approaching a floor, especially in active management?
turns.zh: 对投资者而言是这样的。不过就费用来说，指数基金并不会给公司带来太多收入……我是说，管理任何基金显然都需要钱。但主动型基金的费用要用来支付研究、投资组合管理、分销以及业务的其他所有方面。那么，你是否看到费率压缩正接近一个下限的迹象，尤其是在主动管理领域？

turns.en: So... You know, my view is that right now what we're seeing is a slowing in this long run decline in fees rather than kind of approaching a hard floor. You know, it's true that after decades of steady declines, expense ratios for actively managed equity mutual funds have flattened somewhat in recent years. You know, this suggests that many of the easiest opportunities for fee reductions have already been realized. But Looking ahead and just thinking about technological innovation and operational efficiencies, I really believe there's still room for further rate reductions over time. Advancements in technology and AI have the potential to improve efficiency in portfolio management, back office operations, compliance, reporting, and other administrative functions. To the extent those efficiencies lower the cost of running the active funds, competitive pressures will force those savings to be passed along to investors.
turns.zh: 嗯……我的观点是，我们现在看到的是这一长期费率下行趋势的放缓，而不是接近一个硬性的下限。的确，在经历了数十年的稳步下降之后，主动管理型股票共同基金的费用率近年来有所趋平。这表明许多最容易实现的降费机会已经被用尽。但展望未来，仅从技术创新和运营效率的角度考虑，我确实相信随着时间推移仍有进一步降费的空间。技术和人工智能的进步有潜力提高投资组合管理、后台运营、合规、报告及其他行政职能的效率。如果这些效率提升降低了运作主动型基金的成本，竞争压力将迫使这些节省被转交给投资者。

turns.en: Okay. On the same note, I know when I entered the industry, there was still a ton of money going into load funds. And I think a lot of ETF investors have no idea what a load is. But, you know, do you think the shift away from loads and even 12B1 fees, towards more fee-based, you know, you think it's changed the economics of the mutual fund industry and the way we should think about the cost investors actually pay for investment management?
turns.zh: 好的。顺着这个话题，我知道我刚入行时，还有大量资金流入前端收费基金（load funds）。我想很多 ETF 投资者根本不知道“申购费”是什么。那么，你认为从申购费甚至 12b-1 费用转向更多收费型（fee-based）模式，是否改变了共同基金行业的经济学，以及我们思考投资者为投资管理实际支付成本的方式？

turns.en: I think one of the clearest signs we've seen of how the fund industry has evolved over, you know, over the last few decades is that today over 90% of long-term mutual fund sales go to no-load funds without 12b1 fees. So there is very, very little being sold through the mutual fund channel with, you know, certainly with a load and or even a 12b1 fee. And as you noted, you know, that is up dramatically from previous decades. But that doesn't necessarily mean investors are paying nothing for advice. So when you think about, you know, the cost of what investors actually pay, you have to remember that some of that load, some of that 12B1 fee really was being diverted to the financial advisor. And that's not happening anymore. Financial advisors have changed their compensation models. They're being paid directly. uh, by investors now, um, not through 12B1 fees and, but you can't just say, oh, you know, invest that and just look at the fund expense ratios. You have to also consider the cost of advice and that advice now is being charged separately from the fund. Um, So, you know, when you're looking at costs, it's important to look beyond the fund expense ratio.
turns.zh: 我认为，我们看到的关于基金行业在过去几十年如何演变的最清晰迹象之一就是：如今超过 90% 的长期共同基金销售额流向了没有 12b-1 费用的免申购费基金（no-load funds）。所以通过共同基金渠道销售的、带申购费和/或 12b-1 费用的产品已经非常非常少了。正如你指出的，这相比前几十年有了巨大的提升。但这并不必然意味着投资者没有为投资建议付费。所以当你思考投资者实际支付的成本时，你必须记住，其中一部分申购费、一部分 12b-1 费用实际上是被转移给了财务顾问。而现在这种情况不再发生了。财务顾问已经改变了他们的薪酬模式，现在是由投资者直接付费给他们，而不是通过 12b-1 费用。但你不能只是说“哦，就投资那只基金”，然后只看基金的费用率。你还必须考虑投资建议的成本，而这部分费用现在是与基金分开收取的。所以，在考察成本时，重要的是要看到基金费用率之外的东西。

turns.en: No, yeah, I think it definitely makes it more transparent and beneficial to the investors or end investors. You know, earlier we talked about advisors and investors kind of combining both passive and active in the same portfolio. You know, but we've also noticed that a lot of ETF-owning households also own mutual funds. So, Just curious what your research tells us, how investors are actually using those two vehicles together in the same portfolio.
turns.zh: 是的，我认为这确实让它对投资者、或者说终端投资者更加透明、更有利。前面我们谈到顾问和投资者会把被动和主动结合在同一个组合里。但我们也注意到，很多持有 ETF 的家庭同样持有共同基金。所以我很好奇，你们的研究告诉我们，投资者实际上是如何在同一个组合中一起使用这两种载体的？

turns.en: I think, you know, and you hit on it. One of the most interesting findings from ICI's research is that ETF investors are rarely ETF-only investors. In fact, 86% of ETF-owning households also own mutual funds. And so when we look at that, and I had one of my team members pull some data on this. So when we look at that group, that group of households that own both mutual funds and ETS, and what we're finding there is that mutual funds are heavily used in retirement saving. So roughly three quarters of this group of people or households own mutual funds through their employer-sponsored retirement plans, and ownership rates inside workplace retirement plans exceed 80% for many working-age households. Mutual fund ownership inside IRAs is also high, and that's true even for households younger than 35. So 65% of these households, and they own ETFs as well, own mutual funds inside their IRAs, outside retirement plans and IRAs. So think about like... taxable brokerage accounts, only about half of these younger households own mutual funds. While over 65% of households over 65 own them in their taxable sort of brokerage accounts or taxable accounts. And when we look at ETF ownership rates, they're very stable across the age groups. And that's both in IRAs and taxable brokerage accounts. So about 60% of households that own both products, mutual funds and ETFs, hold ETFs in their taxable brokerage accounts and a similar share hold ETFs in their IRAs. Interesting. And if we think about that, going back to the younger households, that means when we combine this data together, those younger households, the ones younger than 35, in their IRA, they're holding both mutual funds and ETFs.
turns.zh: 我觉得——你正好说到了这一点。ICI 研究中最有意思的发现之一是，ETF 投资者很少是只持有 ETF 的投资者。事实上，86% 持有 ETF 的家庭也持有共同基金。当我们观察这个群体时——我让团队的一位成员提取了一些相关数据——我们发现，在同时持有共同基金和 ETF 的这一组家庭中，共同基金被大量用于退休储蓄。因此，这组人群或家庭中大约四分之三通过雇主发起的退休计划持有共同基金，而且在许多处于工作年龄的家庭中，职场退休计划内部的持有率超过 80%。IRA 内部的共同基金持有率也很高，即便对于 35 岁以下的家庭也是如此：这些家庭中有 65%（他们同时也持有 ETF）在其 IRA 中持有共同基金。在退休计划和 IRA 之外，比如应税经纪账户，这些较年轻的家庭中只有约一半持有共同基金；而 65 岁以上的家庭中，超过 65% 在其应税经纪账户或应税账户中持有共同基金。当我们观察 ETF 持有率时，它们在各年龄组之间非常稳定，无论是在 IRA 还是应税经纪账户中都是如此：在同时持有共同基金和 ETF 这两种产品的家庭中，约 60% 在其应税经纪账户中持有 ETF，类似比例的家庭在其 IRA 中持有 ETF。有意思。如果我们把这一点与较年轻的家庭联系起来，那就意味着，当我们把这些数据合并起来看，35 岁以下的年轻家庭在他们的 IRA 中同时持有共同基金和 ETF。

turns.en: So I guess it means the mutual fund's not dead, at least not yet.
turns.zh: 所以我猜这意味着共同基金并没有死，至少现在还没有。

turns.en: Definitely not.
turns.zh: 绝对没有。

turns.en: And so, yeah, one of the big questions I want to ask before, we're going to have one more after this, but Beyond cost, what does the research tell us about what investors actually value when selecting funds? Has that changed as ETFs have become a larger part of the market?
turns.zh: 那么，是的，在结束之前我想问一个大问题——这之后我们还会有一个：除了成本之外，关于投资者在挑选基金时真正看重什么，研究告诉了我们什么？随着 ETF 在市场中占据更大份额，这一点是否发生了变化？

turns.en: So ETF and mutual funds, the mutual fund investors consider a wide variety of factors, but at the top of their lists are historical performance, the risks associated with the fund, and the investment objective of the fund. So also these, you know, what's interesting is these are valued. We might think about it as valued quite similarly between mutual fund investors and ETF investors. So, you know, I'm just going to give you an example. Eighty nine percent of mutual fund investors say historical performance is important when considering a fund purchase. 89% of ETF investors say historical performance is important when considering a mutual fund purchase. Now, you know, this, this result may not be that surprising since there's so much overlap in mutual fund in ETF ownership, right? We, we just finished talking about how investors own both products. Um, And I think also because there's so much overlap, we really haven't noticed any significant changes in these rankings or percentages over time. They're pretty stable. Okay.
turns.zh: 就 ETF 和共同基金而言，共同基金投资者会考虑各种各样的因素，但排在他们清单最前面的是历史业绩、与该基金相关的风险，以及基金的投资目标。有意思的是，这些因素在共同基金投资者和 ETF 投资者之间的受重视程度可以说非常相似。我举个例子：89% 的共同基金投资者表示，在考虑购买基金时历史业绩很重要；89% 的 ETF 投资者表示，在考虑购买共同基金时历史业绩很重要。这个结果可能并不那么令人意外，因为共同基金与 ETF 的持有存在大量重叠，对吧？我们刚刚才谈完投资者同时持有这两种产品。我认为也正因为重叠度这么高，我们确实没有注意到这些排名或百分比随时间出现任何显著变化。它们相当稳定。好的。

turns.en: And I just have one more question before I let you go. If we think about the future, if we're having this conversation, say, five years from now, what do you think will change the most about active management? The vehicles investors use, what they pay, where they buy funds, or even something else entirely?
turns.zh: 在放你走之前我还有最后一个问题。如果我们展望未来，假设五年后我们再进行这场对话，你认为主动管理变化最大的会是什么？是投资者使用的载体、他们支付的费用、他们购买基金的渠道，还是完全另有其他？

turns.en: So if we were having this conversation five years from now, I think the biggest change would be how active management is delivered, accessed, and implemented. So we're already seeing active management migrate into ETF wrappers, and that trend has accelerated dramatically in recent years. You know, as advisors, model portfolios, individual investors increasingly adopt active ETFs. At the same time, Tokenization could create new ways to package and distribute investment products, potentially allowing investors to access strategies through more flexible, customized, and digitally native channels. Another, and I talked a little bit about this, and another factor is artificial intelligence could be equally transformative. On the investment side, AI can has the potential to improve research, portfolio construction, risk management, and operational efficiency. On the distribution side, AI-powered advice and portfolio tools could make sophisticated investment solutions available to a much broader set of investors. And as these efficiency reduce costs, competition is likely to continue passing on those savings to investors.
turns.zh: 如果我们在五年后进行这场对话，我认为最大的变化会是主动管理的交付方式、获取方式和实施方式。我们已经看到主动管理向 ETF 外壳迁移，而这一趋势近年来显著加速，因为顾问的模型组合和个人投资者越来越多地采用主动型 ETF。与此同时，代币化（tokenization）可能创造出包装和分销投资产品的新方式，有可能让投资者通过更灵活、更定制化、数字原生的渠道获得各种策略。另一个因素——我前面稍微谈到过——是人工智能，它同样可能带来变革。在投资端，AI 有潜力改进研究、组合构建、风险管理和运营效率；在分销端，AI 驱动的投顾和组合工具可以让复杂的投资解决方案为更广泛的投资者所获得。而随着这些效率提升降低成本，竞争很可能会继续把这些节省传递给投资者。

turns.en: Well, it'll be interesting to watch and see what happens. But we need to end here. But this was great, Shelley. Thank you again for joining me today.
turns.zh: 嗯，看看会发生什么会很有意思。但我们必须到此结束了。这期节目非常棒，Shelly。再次感谢你今天与我对话。

turns.en: Yeah, thank you so much.
turns.zh: 是的，非常感谢。
